definition: An informal social contract among Spire residents and upper-tier corponation employees to mutually suppress, deny, or redirect public attention away from scandals that could destabilize shared financial interests. Not written, rarely spoken aloud, universally understood.
origin: Corporate jargon, derived ironically from old religious covenant language; likely originated in Palladian Group boardrooms
usage: Tier 4-5 and Spire executives; referenced with contempt by investigative journalists and Tier 1-2 dissidents
example: The environmental report never surfaced — gilt covenant, everyone assumed, because three corponations had fingers in the same aquifer.
